newsitem.title: UK: BP signs oil search deal with Mozambique.
newsitem.headline: BP signs oil search deal with Mozambique.

text.p: The British Petroleum Co Plc has signed a memorandum of understanding with state-owned ENH-Hidrocarbonetos de Macambique granting BP exclusive rights to explore an area of up to 40,000 square kilometres in Mozambique's Zambesi Delta, a BP spokesman said on Tuesday.
The spokesman told Reuters BP would "shortly commence" a technical study of the existing data held by ENH. The study should take about six months and covers an area of 80,000 square kilometers.

BP would then decide whether to proceed with a second phase of two-dimensional seismic work covering 40,000 square kilometers. Negotiations over a production sharing agreement would be conducted during the second phase, the spokesman said.
If the second phase were successful, the BP official said, three-dimensional seismic work and drilling "could follow."
Although commercial oil has not been found in Mozambique, only four wells have been drilled, the BP official said.

"They were drilled in the 1970s without the benefit of the latest exploration technology. We're hopeful but it is early to speculate on the chances of success," the BP official said. In Africa, BP is active in upstream oil projects in Nigeria and Angola.

Enron Corp of the United States is involved in the Pande gas project in Mozambique which could be onstream by 2000 provided a number of trade and fiscal changes are made, an Enron official said recently.
